Estimate sample orderings and smooth feature trajectories

Source: R/07_mpcurve.R
fit_mpcurve.Rd

Fits a Gaussian trajectory model to a sample-by-feature matrix. With intrinsic_dim = 1, all features share one latent sample ordering. With intrinsic_dim = M >= 2, the model estimates M orderings and a probability distribution over orderings for each feature. Random-walk priors encourage smooth trajectories, and variational inference estimates uncertainty in both sample positions and feature trajectories.

Usage

fit_mpcurve(
  X,
  algorithm = c("cavi", "csmooth_em", "smooth_em"),
  method = c("PCA", "fiedler", "pcurve", "tSNE", "random", "isomap"),
  K = NULL,
  rw_q = 2,
  lambda = 1,
  S = NULL,
  sigma2_init = NULL,
  fix_lambda = FALSE,
  iter = 100,
  tol = 1e-06,
  num_cores = 1L,
  intrinsic_dim = 1L,
  greedy = c("none", "forward", "backward"),
  partition_init = c("similarity", "ordering_methods"),
  discretization = NULL,
  ridge = 0,
  lambda_sd_prior_rate = NULL,
  lambda_min = 1e-10,
  lambda_max = 1e+10,
  sigma_min = 1e-10,
  sigma_max = 1e+10,
  position_prior = c("adaptive", "fixed"),
  position_prior_init = NULL,
  partition_prior = c("adaptive", "fixed"),
  partition_prior_init = NULL,
  effective_weight_tol = 1e-12,
  assignment_prior = NULL,
  ordering_alpha = NULL,
  similarity_metric = c("spearman", "pearson", "smooth_fit"),
  smooth_fit_lambda_mode = c("optimize", "fixed"),
  smooth_fit_lambda_value = 1,
  cluster_linkage = "single",
  similarity_min_feature_sd = 1e-08,
  T_start = 5,
  T_end = 1,
  n_outer = 25L,
  inner_iter = 1L,
  max_converge_iter = NULL,
  tol_outer = 1e-05,
  freeze_unused_ordering = NULL,
  freeze_unused_ordering_threshold = NULL,
  freeze_feature = NULL,
  freeze_feature_weight_threshold = NULL,
  drop_unused_ordering = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

X

Numeric matrix (n x d), with samples in rows and features in columns.

algorithm

Fitting algorithm. Use "cavi" for coordinate-ascent variational inference, the supported fitting method.

method

Initialisation method(s) for the trajectory ordering. In the single-ordering case, multiple methods are all attempted only when num_cores > 1; otherwise only method[[1]] is fitted. For partition fits, length(method) must be either 1 or intrinsic_dim.

K

Integer number of mixture components (grid knots).

rw_q

Integer random-walk order for the GMRF prior.

lambda

Positive initial smoothness value(s). A single-ordering fit accepts a scalar or length-d vector. A structural partition fit accepts a scalar, a length-d vector broadcast across orderings, a flattened length-d * M vector, or a d x M matrix.

S

Optional known measurement standard deviations. If a length-d vector, each feature uses a known shared standard deviation across observations. If an n x d matrix, each observation-feature pair uses its own known standard deviation.

sigma2_init

Optional scalar or length-d initial variance vector. Partition fits use one vector shared across all orderings. It cannot be supplied together with S.

fix_lambda

Logical; if TRUE, keep all smoothness parameters fixed at the supplied initial value.

iter

Maximum number of CAVI sweeps for the single-ordering fit.

tol

Relative ELBO tolerance for the single-ordering CAVI fit.

num_cores

Integer >= 1. Workers for parallel multi-method single-ordering runs.

intrinsic_dim

Integer intrinsic dimensionality of the latent ordering system. intrinsic_dim = 1 fits the standard single-ordering model. Values >= 2 fit the fixed-\(M\) structural partition model.

greedy

Use "none"; specify the number of orderings through intrinsic_dim. The values "forward" and "backward" are unsupported.

partition_init

For partition fits only: either "similarity" for feature-similarity-driven block initialization or "ordering_methods" for method-based initial orderings. The default is "similarity".

discretization

Optional discretization method passed to ordering-based initialization. For partition fits, MPCurver enforces a common K across orderings; if quantile cuts collapse, it falls back to equal-width bins.

ridge

Nonnegative diagonal term added to the random-walk precision. The default 0 uses an intrinsic prior, with the likelihood identifying directions unpenalized by the prior. A positive value gives a proper Gaussian prior. An identifiability error indicates that the likelihood and prior together leave some trajectory directions undetermined.

lambda_sd_prior_rate

Optional positive rate for an exponential prior on 1 / sqrt(lambda_j). Larger rates encourage smoother trajectories. The default NULL, or 0, applies no additional penalty to the smoothness parameter.

lambda_min, lambda_max

Positive bounds for lambda_j.

sigma_min, sigma_max

Positive bounds for sigma_j^2. Structural partition fits update one feature-specific vector shared across orderings.

position_prior

Either "adaptive" or "fixed" for the single-ordering component prior pi. Partition fits apply the same mode independently to each ordering's position responsibilities.

position_prior_init

Optional length-K initial/fixed vector for the component prior pi. When position_prior = "fixed" and this is NULL, a uniform prior over the K positions is used. For intrinsic_dim > 1, a single length-K vector is broadcast to all orderings.

partition_prior

For partition fits only: either "adaptive" or "fixed" for the ordering-usage prior omega. The adaptive mode uses an empirical-Bayes update proportional to colSums(w). The fixed mode keeps a constant prior over the fixed set of \(M\) orderings.

partition_prior_init

For partition fits only: optional length-M initial/fixed vector for the ordering prior omega. Used only when partition_prior = "fixed". When omitted, the fixed prior defaults to uniform over the \(M\) orderings.

effective_weight_tol

Nonnegative threshold for reporting the effective number of orderings under partition_prior = "adaptive". An ordering counts when its fitted prior mass \(\omega_m\) exceeds this threshold. The default is 1e-12; the value must be less than 1 / intrinsic_dim. It does not change the fitted model. The result stores the threshold in $effective_weight_tol for partition fits.

assignment_prior

Deprecated; use partition_prior and partition_prior_init. The value "uniform" specifies a fixed uniform prior; "dirichlet" specifies a Dirichlet prior using ordering_alpha.

ordering_alpha

Dirichlet concentration for the deprecated assignment_prior = "dirichlet" option.

similarity_metric

For partition_init = "similarity" only: feature-similarity metric used to construct feature blocks. One of "spearman", "pearson", or "smooth_fit". The "smooth_fit" metric scores how well features follow each other's orderings under a random-walk smoother. With ridge = 0, this score uses the rank and generalized determinant of the intrinsic precision. With positive ridge, it uses a proper Gaussian prior.

smooth_fit_lambda_mode

For similarity_metric = "smooth_fit" only: whether the directional smoother optimizes lambda or keeps it fixed at smooth_fit_lambda_value.

smooth_fit_lambda_value

For similarity_metric = "smooth_fit" only: fixed lambda value used when smooth_fit_lambda_mode = "fixed", and the starting value when smooth_fit_lambda_mode = "optimize".

cluster_linkage

For partition_init = "similarity" only: hierarchical-clustering linkage applied to 1 - S(X). Defaults to "single".

similarity_min_feature_sd

For partition_init = "similarity" only: low-variance feature threshold used when building S(X).

T_start, T_end

Positive starting and ending temperatures for the feature-assignment annealing schedule. Higher temperatures encourage more diffuse assignments during initialization. After this schedule, fitting continues at \(T=1\). Assess convergence in that final segment; changing the temperature changes the objective.

n_outer

Number of annealing steps for partition CAVI.

inner_iter

Number of structural coordinate sweeps per annealing step.

max_converge_iter

Maximum number of exact T = 1 partition iterations after annealing. Defaults to iter when NULL.

tol_outer

Relative objective tolerance for partition convergence after annealing.

freeze_unused_ordering, freeze_unused_ordering_threshold, freeze_feature, freeze_feature_weight_threshold, drop_unused_ordering

Deprecated; leave as NULL. Explicit values are ignored with a warning.

verbose

Logical; print per-iteration progress?

...

Additional variational fitting options, including initialization controls such as responsibilities_init, fits_init, init_methods, pca_components, or hard_assign_final.

Value

An mpcurve object, or (for parallel multi-method single-ordering runs) a named list whose successful entries are mpcurve objects and whose failed entries are NULL. The list has a summary attribute recording success, convergence, final ELBO, and any error message for every attempted method. Every returned fit stores inferred cell locations in $locations; for single-ordering fits this includes both posterior-mean and MAP locations derived from $gamma. A structural partition result stores named ordering-specific $params$pi, $params$mu, $gamma, and $locations; one shared $params$sigma2; $conditional_posterior; a d x M $lambda_mat; and $partition$pi_weights. Every fit has $effective_intrinsic_dim; adaptive partition fits calculate it from the fitted ordering prior using effective_weight_tol, while other fits set it to the fitted M. See mpcurve for the complete object description.

Details

The latent grid has K ordered positions. Each sample has a posterior probability of occupying each position, and each feature has a Gaussian trajectory posterior across the grid. Noise variances are estimated per feature unless measurement standard deviations are supplied through S.

For \(M \ge 2\), structural variational inference uses $$q(C)\prod_{j=1}^d q(Z_j)q(U_j\mid Z_j).$$ Here \(C\) denotes the sample positions across orderings, \(Z_j\) is feature \(j\)'s ordering assignment, and \(U_j\) is its trajectory. Conditioning the trajectory on the assignment preserves their posterior dependence. Smoothness parameters vary by feature and ordering; the estimated noise variance \(\sigma_j^2\) is shared across orderings.

The number of orderings M is specified by intrinsic_dim and held fixed during fitting. Choose it using the scientific question and assess the stability and interpretation of the resulting feature groups. The variational objective measures progress for a given M; comparing different values requires a separate model-selection criterion.

Use summary() to inspect the fit, plot() to visualize sample orderings and trajectories, and do_mpcurve to run additional iterations. See mpcurve for the fitted-object fields.
